svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Comparison of logarithmic denominator growth in classical-constant models
svg.desc: Line chart. Horizontal axis: position N on a logarithmic scale from 32 to 4096. Vertical axis: log of the reduced denominator divided by N, from 0 to 1.1. Thin dotted reference lines mark the theorem rates 1, 2/3, 1/2 and 1/3. A solid grey curve for the standard ln 2 series fluctuates between about 0.8 and 1 and settles near 0.99, near rate 1. A dash-dot curve for arctan(1/2), marked paper-only, settles near 2/3. A dashed curve for the half-rate ln 2 series and open circles for ln(4/3) nearly coincide and approach 1/2. A dotted curve for ln(8/7) approaches 1/3. A violet shaded region along the bottom, bounded by 3 log N / N, shrinks toward zero and marks the denominators allowed by the rational-prefix certificate.
svg.text: q(N) is the reduced denominator of the shifted binary prefix at position N; natural log
Dotted horizontal lines: theorem rates. Every point is an exact reduced denominator (Fraction arithmetic).
Outside the certificate's hypotheses; no conclusion about normality of ln 2. Half-rate series: CC-01. Certificate: AC-01.
